transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2025-04-22 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~62 min | Recorded by Fireflies
Attendees (as recorded): Maya Chen, Ethan Zhao, Samir Patel (Redwood) — Jordan Blake, Priya Ramesh, Luis Morales, Avery Kim (CloudScale Retail)

Summary:
Redwood and CloudScale Retail kickoff a POC focused on workload characterization and traffic modeling to size Dedicated capacity and prove latency/cost targets. Customer needs: real-world QPS/concurrency modeling, input/output token distributions, 90th/95th latency SLOs, and guidance on caching/quantization tradeoffs. Agreed next steps include a 24h benchmark comparing Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated with provided sample prompts and a follow-up security/infra review.

Topics covered:
- What 'success' looks like (latency SLOs, cost per 1M tokens, quality thresholds)
- Current prod traffic profile and spikes (avg QPS, peak QPS, concurrency)
- Typical input/output token lengths and heavy-tail outliers
- Benchmark design: synthetic vs replay, duration, percentiles to measure
- Sizing recommendation for Dedicated pool and fallback routing
- Security/VPC/KMS constraints and audit log needs

--- Transcript (timestamps approximate, auto-transcription includes occasional errors) ---
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Ok everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros then jump into traffic and success criteria — Jordan, want to kick off with why you're running this POC?
[00:18] Jordan (CloudScale CTO): Yeah thanks, uh so our main goal is to move from a proof-of-concept on a single model to something we can run at low-latency in prod. We need to understand how many GPUs to reserve and what latency we can promise to merchants. Right now it's a mix of hosted APIs and a home-grown batch service, but it's inconsistent.
[00:36] Priya (ML Eng): The workload is mostly chat completions for conversational support plus some reranking for search. Typical session has a few messages, average input tokens around 110–140, output around 70–120 but we have long tail prompts from power users up to 2k tokens.
[00:53] Maya: That's super helpful. Do you have numbers for QPS and concurrency—like steady-state and peak?
[00:58] Jordan: Avg is small—around 3 req/s globally. Peaks push to 15–18 qps during flash sales; concurrency can hit 8–12 on the worst day. Note these are user-facing, so 95th percentile latency under 500ms is kind of our bar.
[01:18] Ethan (Redwood SE): Quick clarifying question — when you say concurrency 8–12, is that concurrent in-flight requests per model replica, or total across all tenants?
[01:26] Luis (SRE): Total across our product instances. We'll need isolation for traffic from certain merchants, so tenancy and routing matter—multi-tenant separation is a hard requirement.
[01:36] Samir (Redwood Solutions): For isolation, Dedicated pools with tenant pinning is usually our recommendation. We can also do routing rules to fallback to hosted if Dedicated is saturated.
[01:45] Maya: For the POC success criteria — what will make you say yes? Latency, cost, and model output quality?
[01:52] Avery (Product): Exactly. We need 95th below 600ms for the smallest/most-frequent prompts, cost below our current provider by at least 20% per 1M tokens, and parity on quality — outputs must not regress on our golden prompt set.
[02:09] Priya: On quality, we will provide a golden set and some acceptance criteria (F1-like metrics for entity extraction, and manual spot checks for chat tone).
[02:18] Ethan: Great—so benchmark design wise we should run both replay of real traffic and synthetic variations (to stress long prompts). We suggest a 24h run to capture diurnal patterns, with isolated bursts to simulate flash sales.
[02:31] Jordan: That works. How do you want the sample payloads formatted? We have JSON logs with prompt_text, user_id, timestamp, and latency to upstream.
[02:40] Ethan: JSON is perfect. Please also include token counts if possible, and label the prompts by intent (chat, rerank, assist) so we can weight them correctly in the replay.
[02:50] Maya: For sizing, based on the numbers you gave (avg 3 QPS, peaks 15–18, concurrency up to 12), a preliminary recommendation would be a Dedicated pool sized for peak tail with autoscale buffers. Samir, you mentioned 4x A10G recommendation?
[03:05] Samir: Right — assuming the canonical open model you're evaluating (2.7B-ish family) and standard FP16/quantized flow, 4x A10G equiv should hit your 95th in the target range if KV cache is warm. If you anticipate many unique prefixes, you'll need higher GPU headroom.
[03:22] Priya: We do have lots of new sessions (un-cached prefixes) during onboarding campaigns — so warm cache assumptions are risky.
[03:29] Maya: Good flag. Then part of POC should explicitly test cold cache scenarios. We'll include cache-warm and cold buckets in the workload.
[03:37] Jordan: How do you measure token-level cost? We need per-token breakdowns and a projection for monthly spend at projected traffic.
[03:45] Ethan: Benchmarks will output tokens/second, tokens/req, and per-token CPU/GPU time. We'll synthesize cost models with your reserved pool price + per-token hosted price to generate monthly cost under different hit rates for cache and batch sizes.
[03:58] Luis: On security — we require SOC2, SAML SSO, VPC peering, and KMS integration. We may run the Dedicated control plane inside our VPC. Is that supported?
[04:09] Maya: Yes — Redwood Private supports VPC deployment and KMS/HSM integrations. For the POC we can run tests through our hosted offering with VPC peering or a short-term dedicated tunnel. We'll also send our security pack.
[04:20] Priya: Will audit logs include token-level metadata or just request IDs? We need to ensure PII isn't retained.
[04:26] Samir: By default we offer request-level logs and can redact prompt text on ingest. We'll include token counts and latency but strip prompt content if you request. We'll surface an audit log schema in the security doc.
[04:38] Jordan: OK. Benchmarks — can we compare Hosted vs Dedicated in the same run? We want to see cost/latency delta.
[04:45] Ethan: Yes, we can orchestrate parallel runs: run sample traffic against Hosted endpoints and also against a Dedicated pool configured to match model and quantization. We'll keep configs identical aside from the backend.
[04:55] Avery: Timeline expectations? We want to present to execs in two weeks. Is that realistic?
[04:59] Maya: Two weeks is tight but doable for a high-level comparison. For a thorough 24h benchmark and security review, plan for three to five business days to gather artifacts and run the runs, then follow-up. We should aim to have initial numbers in ~3 business days.
[05:14] Priya: About input/output token distribution — our histogram is heavy-tailed. Most prompts are under 150 tokens, 5% are 500–1k, and ~0.5% exceed 1.5k. We need to ensure percentile metrics capture these tails.
[05:29] Ethan: We'll include p50/p90/p95/p99 token-length buckets and correlate latency by token-length. Also report batching efficiency (tokens per batch) and effect of prefix caching on per-token GPU time.
[05:41] Jordan: Any constraints for the bench harness? We have private subnets and can't easily egress to public endpoints for the Dedicated-run; would Redwood be able to run agents from our VPC?
[05:51] Samir: We can run a small runner inside your VPC or do a temporary peering. We'll coordinate with Luis on access and firewall rules.
[05:58] Luis: We'll need an IP allowlist and short-lived creds for the runner. Also request all test traffic be labeled and rotated so it's clearly marked in logs.
[06:07] Maya: Noted. We'll provide a runner image and instructions, plus short-lived creds for the repo.
[06:12] Avery: On acceptance criteria — besides latency and cost, we also need a quality gate. Priya will run golden-set comparisons. If we see >5% regression in extraction F1 or repeated hallucinations, it fails.
[06:24] Priya: We'll do both automated diffs and manual review for chat quality. We'll provide examples where hallucination is unacceptable.
[06:30] Ethan: We'll also capture generation tokens distribution and check for truncation or stop-token variance.
[06:35] Jordan: What's the fallback plan in prod if Dedicated saturates? We must not drop traffic.
[06:40] Maya: Redwood's smart routing can route overflow to a compatible hosted variant automatically. For the POC we'll test that path to quantify latency delta.
[06:48] Jordan: Perfect. Anything else?
[06:51] Samir: One more item — quantization profiles. If you want aggressive 4-bit quantization, include a quality regression bucket. We'll measure throughput improvements vs quality.
[06:59] Priya: Include that.
[07:01] Maya: OK recap and concrete next steps — we'll share the security docs, provide runner image and bench harness, Redwood runs the initial 24h benchmark comparing Hosted/Dedicated, and customer provides prompt corpus and histograms. Follow-up meeting 2025-04-29 to review.
[07:16] Jordan: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[07:19] Maya: Thanks — we'll circulate notes and action items.

End of call.
